big_idea: Plan a PARTY: pick items, total cost, pay, calculate change!
learning_intention: We are learning to plan a budget and calculate change.
student_learning_goal: I can plan a budget and calculate change.
success_criteria: I can PAY with right money.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Pat + Bea — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.hook: Pat + Bea: Today plan a PARTY with $20! Pick items, total, pay, calculate change! Pat + Bea open: 'Estimate, EXACT, CENTS, MIXED — that's BUDGETING!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Money friends — today is our CAPSTONE. On Day 1 we ESTIMATED with Pat. On Day 2 Bea showed EXACT change. Day 3 we did CENTS. Day 4 we mixed them. Today we put it all together to plan a party!

Bring children to the carpet. Pat and Bea puppets in party hats. 'Money friends — today is our CAPSTONE. We plan a PARTY!'

Define new words. 'BUDGET = a PLAN for spending. TOTAL = ADD all together.'

Demo. 'My budget: $20 for a party. I pick 4 items:'
- Maple cookies $4.
- Hockey balloons $5.
- Tim Hortons donuts $7.
- Drinks $3.

Total: $4 + $5 + $7 + $3 = $19.

'Pay $20. Change: $20 - $19 = $1!'

'Pat says — the BUDGET is the LIMIT!'

Demo a wrong plan. 'If I pick items totaling $25 — over budget!'

'Bea says — total must be ≤ budget!'

Now show the 4 stations:
- Station 1: PICK 4 items from 16.
- Station 2: TOTAL all 4 prices.
- Station 3: PAY with bills (at least $20).
- Station 4: CALCULATE change.

Each child rotates 5 min per station and records on TEMPLATE.

'Pat + Bea say — be a PARTY PLANNER!'

steps.instruction: Hand out templates. 4 stations rotation (~5 min each).
Stretch: write a 'planner's brag' — sentence per station.
STRATEGY COMPARE: Two pairs share their party plans for the same budget. Class compares: same items? same total? Cite Carpenter & Moser CGI separate-result-unknown.
steps.teacher_prompt: Pat: 'Same budget, different parties. The MATH says: total ≤ budget.'

differentiation.for_movement_learners: Walk between 4 stations physically. NO-PAPER VERSION: children plan the party orally with running total on fingers; teacher records on chart paper.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Four signals: pick; total; pay; change.

consolidation.exit_routine: Capstone refrain — Pat + Bea call: 'Estimate, EXACT, CENTS, MIXED — that's BUDGETING!' (3x). Each child shares their party plan + total spent.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child plans the party but reports the PRICE as the change — repairing the change-direction confusion
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On the party capstone, the trap is overshooting the budget: child plans without tracking cumulative cost, OR computes change wrong by reporting price instead of money-paid - price. Carpenter & Moser CGI 'separate result unknown' vs 'compare difference unknown' frames the change-direction confusion.

Today integrates Lessons 1-4: estimate (L1), exact change (L2), cents (L3), mixed amounts (L4) into a peer party-planning case.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Pat asks — what's your BUDGET? $20. Your TOTAL? $25. Over budget!'

Guide. 'Remove an item. $25 - $5 = $20. Now within budget.'

Generalise. 'Pat says — TOTAL must be ≤ BUDGET. Adjust if over!'

If still over: prompt to remove cheapest item until within.
common_misconceptions: Budget is a target. (Repair: budget is a LIMIT.)
Pick all items. (Repair: pick within budget.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child reports price as change: drill 'change = MONEY PAID - PRICE'; child re-computes with sentence frame.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child overshoots budget: 'PAUSE — list items + running total; remove last item if over.'
DIAGNOSTIC C — child can compute but won't justify: force 'I spent ___, the budget was ___; difference is ___.'

parts_outline.task: Pick 4 items from a list of 8 (with prices). Total them.
If total > $20, swap items to stay within budget.
